name: Mauher Slieve

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mauher Slieve is an Irish mythological site. The name translates from Irish as Mother Mountain. The form slieve marks the phonetic English spelling of the older Irish words sliab and sliabh. The mountain lies in the southwestern province of Munster, in County Tipperary. Many Munster peaks carry the names of goddesses, such as Áine and Mis. Mauher Slieve rises at the center of a group of twelve mountains. Each of those twelve peaks bears the name of the goddess Ébhlinne. The hill served as a traditional gathering place for the Celtic harvest feast of Lughnasa. Some recensions of the Book of Invasions name the patroness of the Mother Mountain as Fódla. Fódla ranked among the three great earth goddesses of Ireland.

okr.objective: Document the Irish mythological site Mauher Slieve as the Mother Mountain.
